items.readme:
# fastmint-fcfs

**English** · [Bahasa Indonesia](README.id.md)

**FCFS mint on BNB Smart Chain through Binance Agentic Wallet, landed in a block ±2 seconds after the sale opens.**

A skill for AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenClaw, and any other agent that reads `SKILL.md`) that fires a single mint/claim/buy transaction at the exact moment a sale opens, using a Binance Agentic Wallet (`baw` CLI). No private key on the machine: signing happens in Binance's backend through Developer Mode, the agent only prepares calldata and picks the moment.

```
sale opens (T)    T+0.05s          T+0.6–0.8s        T+1.3–1.5s       T+2.1–2.2s
   │                 │                  │                  │                 │
   ▼                 ▼                  ▼                  ▼                 ▼
 start ───► preview sent ───► simulation OK ───► BROADCASTED ───► in a block
         (NTP clock trigger)    (requestId)     (baw execute)     (receipt)
```

The numbers above were measured 11 Nov 2026 from Indonesia: 3 time-gated dry-runs plus one real mint (Pocket Moons, 2 free NFTs, trigger→receipt 2.0 seconds). The previous sequential version took 5–6 seconds.

---

## Table of contents

1. [How it works](#1-how-it-works)
2. [Installation](#2-installation)
3. [Usage flow](#3-usage-flow)
4. [Command reference](#4-command-reference)
5. [Dynamic arguments](#5-dynamic-arguments)
6. [Safety rails](#6-safety-rails)
7. [Measured numbers](#7-measured-numbers)
8. [Troubleshooting](#8-troubleshooting)
9. [File layout](#9-file-layout)
10. [FAQ](#10-faq)

---

## 1. How it works

### Why the old version was slow

`baw` has no direct-send command for a contract call. The flow is two steps by design: `contract-call preview` (the backend simulates and returns a `requestId`) and then `contract-call execute --requestId`. The old version waited for a public RPC to report a successful `eth_call` (±1 second after the opening block), then previewed, then executed. Every stage waited on the previous one: T+5–6 seconds.

### Three parallel triggers

`fire.js` does not wait on a single signal. During the 3-second **burst** window after the sale opens, three triggers may each launch a preview independently (minimum spacing `--gap` 350ms, at most `--inflight` 3 at a time):

| trigger | when | source |
|---|---|---|
| **clock** | exactly T+0 by the NTP-corrected clock | `sntp` to time.apple.com / pool.ntp.org |
| **head** | the first block with `timestamp ≥ start` is seen | WebSocket `newHeads` (QuikNode, publicnode, drpc) + HTTP polling every 150ms |
| **eth_call OK** | a simulation from the wallet succeeds on one of the 4 fastest RPCs | `eth_call` on tags `latest` and `pending`, every 100ms |

The first preview that comes back with `simulationCode 000000000` is executed immediately, **exactly once**. Other previews still in flight are ignored. Previews that fail because the backend has not seen the opening block yet (error `351805`) are cheap and harmless; the next trigger retries.

Once the burst is over, only **eth_call OK** triggers previews, so a sale that opens late does not burn `--maxPreviews`; the `eth_call` spin keeps watching until `--timeout` (600 seconds).

### The ranked RPC pool

The RPC list is measured at start and re-ranked at T-10s (latency and block lag). From Indonesia: QuikNode 31ms, bloXroute 32ms, 48.club 45ms, official dataseed ±105ms, publicnode ±200ms. Nodes that strip revert data (zon, for example) are left out, because a revert with no data cannot be told apart from "not open yet".

`eth_call` race: the first success wins; a revert **with data** wins (deterministic); a revert with no data only counts after every node has answered and is never treated as fatal.

### Revert classification

Error names are decoded from the contract's Sourcify ABI, a built-in list of common errors, then 4byte. Every name maps to:

- **wait**: `NotStarted`, `NotOpen`, `NotLive`, `TooEarly`, `Paused`, … → keep retrying until `--timeout`
- **fatal**: `SoldOut`, `FreeGone`, `AlreadyClaimed`, `AgentIdRequired`, `NotEligible`, `WrongValue`, `Insufficient…` → stop immediately (±50ms)
- **unknown**: treated as wait until `start + --grace` (10s), fatal after that. Before the opening time only the hard-terminal names (sold/gone/already/agent/eligible/expired) are considered fatal.

Override with `--waitOn <regex>` and `--fatalOn <regex>`.

---

## 2. Installation

### Prerequisites

- **Node.js ≥ 20** (v26 in use). No `npm install`: `ethers` 6.13 is already bundled.
- **Binance Agentic Wallet CLI**: `npm install -g @binance/agentic-wallet@1.12.0`
- **Binance App** with Agentic Wallet and **Developer Mode** on (Agentic Wallet → Settings → Developer Mode). The wallet balance must be under the Developer Mode cap.
- The `binance-agentic-wallet` skill from https://github.com/binance/binance-skills-hub (optional but recommended, for other wallet operations).
- Optional: an **Agent ID** (`yourname.ai`) for mints that require one.

### Installing the skill

Extract the zip, then put the `fastmint-fcfs` folder wherever your agent reads skills from:

```bash
# Claude Code (per project)
mkdir -p .claude/skills && cp -r fastmint-fcfs .claude/skills/

# Claude Code (global)
mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && cp -r fastmint-fcfs ~/.claude/skills/

# skills CLI / .agents (Codex, Cursor, etc.)
mkdir -p .agents/skills && cp -r fastmint-fcfs .agents/skills/
chmod +x fastmint-fcfs/fastmint.sh
```

### Wallet sign-in (once, session lasts 2 days / 48 hours idle)

```bash
baw auth signin --json
```

Open the `urlForWeb` that appears, match the `pairingCode` in the Binance App, approve, then:

```bash
baw auth verify --qrCodeId <qrCodeId> --json
baw wallet status --json      # must be CONNECTED
```

### Checking the environment

```bash
cd fastmint-fcfs
./fastmint.sh bench
```

Expected output: RPC ranking, WebSocket delay, clock offset, `wallet status CONNECTED`, `devMode ON`, BNB balance, Agent ID, three previews in ±0.6s, and a time estimate. All read-only.

### `.env` (premium RPC)

The `.env` file in the skill folder is sourced automatically by `fastmint.sh`:

```bash
FASTMINT_RPCS_EXTRA=https://<premium-endpoint>     # prepended to the pool, still ranked
FASTMINT_WS_EXTRA=wss://<premium-endpoint>         # used for newHeads
```

This repo ships a `.env` with a QuikNode BSC endpoint. The host is masked in every log. Other variables: `FASTMINT_RPCS` (replace the whole pool), `FASTMINT_WS`, `FASTMINT_TZ` (default `Asia/Jakarta`), `FASTMINT_CA` (CA bundle for Node, see troubleshooting).

---

## 3. Usage flow

This is the flow the agent runs when you say **"mint free at 23:00 https://mint-site"**:

```
┌──────────┐    ┌──────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────────┐    ┌──────────┐
│  bench   │───►│  recon   │───►│  fire --dry  │───►│    fire      │───►│  report  │
│ env OK?  │    │ CA, ABI, │    │ 10s rehearsal│    │ background,  │    │ tx, link,│
│ ~10s     │    │ getters, │    │ before open  │    │ 1x execute   │    │ TIMELINE │
│          │    │ calldata │    │ stop at prev │    │              │    │          │
└──────────┘    └──────────┘    └──────────────┘    └──────────────┘    └──────────┘
```

**Step 0, bench** (once per session). `UNCONNECTED` → sign in first. devMode OFF → turn it on in the app.

**Step 1, recon** (~5–10s):

```bash
./fastmint.sh recon https://mint-site            # or --contract 0x... if the CA is known
```

Recon fetches the HTML, the JS bundles, and agent documents (`llms.txt`, `skill.md`, `handbook.md`, …), extracting addresses, chainId, mint function names, ABI signatures, and unix times. It then runs `eth_getCode`, pulls the ABI from Sourcify v2 (or from the site bundle filtered down to selectors that actually exist in the bytecode), reads every view getter (0-arg, `(wallet)`, `(agentId)`), and prints **MINT CANDIDATES** with guessed arguments, calldata, simulation results, a `START HINT` from start getters, and ready-to-use `fire:` commands.

Read from the output: opening time, free supply left, price, per-wallet limit, `agentIdOf(wallet)`, and error names (`SoldOut`, `FreeGone`, …).

**Step 2, rehearsal** (always):

```bash
./fastmint.sh fire --to 0xSALE --data 0x195ad114 --start 23:00 --dry
```

Does everything up to the preview, then stops. Check that the `call = …` line decodes to the right function and arguments. Add `--gateSim` if the call can already be simulated now, so the rehearsal exercises the real time-gated path.

**Step 3, fire** (in the background so the chat stays responsive):

```bash
./fastmint.sh fire --to 0xSALE --data 0x195ad114 --start 23:00 --label project_free
```

**Step 4, report**: tx hash, status, BscScan link, the `TIMELINE` line (T+ offsets for trigger/preview/execute/broadcast/inclusion), what was received, and the log path. If it stopped: the decoded revert name and what it means.

---

## 4. Command reference

### `./fastmint.sh`

| command | purpose |
|---|---|
| `bench` | environment check, read-only |
| `bench --ca` | build `~/.config/certs/system-ca.pem` from the macOS keychain |
| `bench --live` | **send 1 real tx** (USDT `balanceOf`, 0 BNB, gas ±0.00002 BNB) to measure execute. Only with explicit user approval |
| `recon <url> [--contract 0x..] [--wallet 0x..] [--json]` | quick recon, read-only |
| `fire …` | execution (see below) |
| `logs [n]` | tail the last run log |
| `locks` | list execute locks |

### `fire`

```
./fastmint.sh fire --to 0xC (--data 0x... | --sig "fn(type,..)" --args '[..]') [--start <t>] [options]
```

| option | default | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--value <BNB>` | 0 | BNB sent, decimal. Paid mints need an explicit number from the user |
| `--maxValue <BNB>` | | cap. Required when value > 0; rejected if value > cap |
| `--start <t>` | now | unix seconds, `HH:MM[:SS]` WIB, or ISO-8601 |
| `--lead <ms>` | 3000 | start spinning before start |
| `--interval <ms>` | 100 | spacing of the eth_call spin |
| `--clockFire <ms>` | 0 | send a preview at start+ms by the clock; `-1` disables |
| `--burst <ms>` | 3000 | clock+head trigger window after start |
| `--gap <ms>` | 350 | minimum spacing between previews |
| `--inflight <n>` | 3 | maximum parallel previews |
| `--maxPreviews <n>` | 40 | give up after that many failed previews |
| `--timeout <s>` | 600 | keep retrying "not open yet" reverts for this long |
| `--grace <s>` | 10 | Unknown reverts count as wait until start+grace |
| `--once` | | one preview, one execute, no retry |
| `--dry` | | stop before execute (`--noPreview`: before preview) |
| `--gateSim` | | rehearsal: ignore eth_call OK before start |
| `--expectNft <n>` | | execute only if the preview shows exactly n NFTs from `--to` entering the wallet |
| `--noEager` / `--noWs` | | disable the head / WebSocket trigger |
| `--gasLimit <n>` | | forwarded to the preview, only on user request |
| `--from 0x..` | baw wallet | sender address |
| `--abi 0x..` | `--to` | another address whose ABI is used to decode errors |
| `--waitOn` / `--fatalOn <regex>` | | override revert classification |
| `--label <name>` | | log/lock file name |

Examples:

```bash
# free mint at 23:00 WIB, raw calldata
./fastmint.sh fire --to 0xSALE --data 0x195ad114 --start 23:00 --label feg_free

# signature + static arguments
./fastmint.sh fire --to 0xSALE --sig "claimFreeShare()" --start 23:00

# dynamic arguments: Agent ID and deadline re-read on every preview
./fastmint.sh fire --to 0xSALE --sig "mintFree(uint256,uint256,uint256,uint256,address)" \
  --args '["$agentId","1","0","$now+1800","0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"]' --start 21:00

# argument that must match the counter at open time
./fastmint.sh fire --to 0xSALE --sig "mint(uint256)" --args '[{"getter":"totalMinted()","add":1}]' --start 1794330000

# paid mint (user said: 2 shares @0.005 = 0.01 BNB)
./fastmint.sh fire --to 0xSALE --sig "buyWithBnb(uint256,address,uint256)" \
  --args '[2,"0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000000",0]' --value 0.01 --maxValue 0.01 --start 23:00

# already-open mint, ensure 2 NFTs are received
./fastmint.sh fire --to 0xNFT --data 0xa0712d68…0002 --value 0 --expectNft 2
```

---

## 5. Dynamic arguments

Elements in `--args` may be placeholders evaluated **right before every preview**, so values that change at open time are always fresh:

| form | value |
|---|---|
| `"$wallet"` | the baw wallet address on chain 56 |
| `"$agentId"` | Agent ID tokenId = `uint256(keccak256(handle))`, from registry `0x60B9…022F` `handleOf(wallet)` |
| `"$zero"` | `0x000…000` |
| `"$now+1800"` | unix now + 1800 (deadline) |
| `{"getter":"totalMinted()","add":1}` | `eth_call` to a getter on `--to` (tag `pending`), uint256 result + 1 |
| `{"getter":"saleStart()","at":"0x..","mul":2}` | getter on another contract, multiplied by 2 |

Lock files for calls with dynamic arguments key on `to|selector|value`, so the same mint stays locked even as its arguments change.

---

## 6. Safety rails

These are what make the agent safe to run without close supervision. None may be skipped.

1. **Fire only on an explicit user instruction** for this mint ("mint free at 23:00", "gas", "ok"). A link alone is not an instruction.
2. **Free mint = `--value 0`.** Paid mints need the amount the user stated, set as both `--value` and `--maxValue`. Rejected if value > cap, or if value > 0 without a cap.
3. **One broadcast.** `runs/lock_<hash>.json` is written before execute; the same call is refused forever after. Never retry after execute, even if execute errored or the tx reverted. A lock is removed only on a new explicit instruction.
4. **Never `baw auth signin` automatically.** Status not CONNECTED → stop and ask the user. Never ask for a private key, seed phrase, or session token.
5. **Never push through a Binance risk block** (`351803`), a `RISK` flag, or an allowance/authority change in the preview. Stop and report.
6. **Connected wallet only.** Check balance ≥ value + gas before starting.
7. **The preview must pass**: `simulationCode 000000000`, no allowance/authority change, no RISK, native outflow ≤ cap + 0.003 BNB, `parsedTx.amount` = 0 for a 0-value call, `requestId` present, and `--expectNft` when set.
8. **`PENDING_CONFIRMATION`** → the user approves in the app; do not resend.
9. **Premium RPC keys are never printed**: every log carries the host only.

---

## 7. Measured numbers

All from one machine in Indonesia, 11 Nov 2026, over encrypted DNS.

**Components**

| component | value |
|---|---|
| `baw wallet status` (CLI cold start) | 0.3–0.4s |
| `baw contract-call preview` | 0.45–0.8s (requestId valid 300s) |
| `baw contract-call execute` → BROADCASTED | 0.68–0.71s |
| broadcast → receipt | 0.54–0.77s |
| BSC block time | ±0.5s |
| fastest RPC (QuikNode / bloXroute / 48.club) | 31 / 32 / 45 ms |
| WS newHeads delay (QuikNode / publicnode) | median 0.45s / 0.56s, best 0.03s |
| local clock offset vs NTP | +0.1–0.16s (corrected automatically) |

**Real mint, already open** (Pocket Moons `mint(2)`, free, 2 NFTs): eth_call OK +35ms → preview 564ms → execute 683ms → BROADCASTED +1.2s → receipt +0.77s. **Total 2.0s.**

**Time-gated dry-runs, 3 runs** (`--gateSim`):

| run | clock | eth_call OK | head | preview OK |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | T+0.054s | T+0.087s | T+0.503s | T+0.761s |
| 2 | T+0.049s | T+0.084s | T+0.168s | T+0.619s |
| 3 | T+0.049s | T+0.083s | T+0.250s | T+0.736s |

**FCFS projection**: broadcast ≈ **T+1.3–1.5s**, in a block ≈ **T+2.1–2.2s**. If Binance's node only sees the opening block on the second preview, add ±0.4s → T+2.6s. The old version: T+5–6s.

---

## 8. Troubleshooting

| symptom | meaning | action |
|---|---|---|
| `baw wallet status` = `UNCONNECTED` | session expired (2 days idle) | user signs in again; the agent must not do it automatically |
| `351802` / `351804` | Developer Mode off / expired / balance above the cap | turn it on in the Binance App, then retry |
| `351803` `AGENT_DEV_MODE_RISK_BLOCKED` | Binance blocks the contract | stop, show the risk text, do not bypass |
| `351805` `simulation failed` repeatedly | mint not open on Binance's node, or wrong arguments | normal before the opening time; if eth_call has been OK for a while, inspect the preview JSON in `runs/` |
| `NotStarted` forever | wrong opening time | compare the contract getter against the site; is `--timeout` enough? |
| `SoldOut` / `FreeGone` | gone | terminal; do not switch to a paid mint without "ok paid" + an amount |
| `AgentIdRequired` / `NotEligible` | wallet without an Agent ID, or needs the agent argument | use `"$agentId"` |
| `AlreadyClaimed` / `AlreadyTaken` | already done | finished |
| `PaymentLow` / `WrongValue` | value ≠ price × qty | read the price getter, confirm the quantity with the user |
| `PENDING_CONFIRMATION` | tx deemed abnormal | user approves in the app; do not resend |
| execute error / no receipt | | **do not retry**; `baw wallet tx-history --json`, `baw wallet tx-lock --json` |
| `gave up after N previews` | backend keeps failing while eth_call is OK | Binance node state differs from public RPCs, or the arguments are wrong |
| `UNABLE_TO_GET_ISSUER_CERT_LOCALLY` (Node) | Node's CA store does not know the certificate chain | macOS: `./fastmint.sh bench --ca`; elsewhere: `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS=/path/ca.pem` |
| `SSL_ERROR … altnames: internetbaik.telkomsel.com` / DNS answers `internetpositif.id` | the ISP hijacks DNS for binance.com (even queries to 1.1.1.1) | use encrypted DNS (Cloudflare 1.1.1.1 app, DNS-only mode) or a VPN. Do not change the system DNS from the agent |
| slow / rate-limited RPC | | `FASTMINT_RPCS=…` or `FASTMINT_RPCS_EXTRA=…` in `.env` |
| `lock exists` | this call has already been executed | delete `runs/lock_*.json` only on a new user instruction |

---

## 9. File layout

```
fastmint-fcfs/
├── SKILL.md            instructions for the agent (read automatically)
├── README.md           this document (English, the GitHub default)
├── README.id.md        Bahasa Indonesia version
├── fastmint.sh         launcher: bench | recon | fire | logs | locks; sources .env and the CA
├── fire.js             FCFS engine: precheck → wait → 3 triggers → preview → 1x execute → receipt
├── recon.js            quick recon: site + Sourcify + getters + mint candidates + calldata
├── bench.js            environment check; --ca builds the CA bundle; --live 1 test tx (with approval)
├── lib.js              RPC pool & race, WS heads, NTP, revert decoding, baw runner, Agent ID, ABI cache
├── ethers.umd.min.js   ethers 6.13.4 (bundled, no npm install)
├── .env                premium RPC (FASTMINT_RPCS_EXTRA / FASTMINT_WS_EXTRA)
├── .gitignore
├── cache/              downloaded Sourcify ABIs
└── runs/               per-run logs, preview/exec/receipt JSON, lock_*.json
```

Logs: `runs/<stamp>_<label>.log`, WIB timestamps plus `T+x.xxxs` offsets. The last line of every run is `TIMELINE`.

---

## 10. FAQ

**Why not just send the transaction directly with a private key? It is faster.**
True, under 1 second is possible. But this skill is built for Binance Agentic Wallet: no private key on the machine, a daily limit, risk blocks, and in-app approval for abnormal txs. The two-step preview/execute is the price of that safety, and 2 seconds is still far below 5 seconds.

**Can the preview be done before the sale opens so only execute remains?**
No. The backend simulates at preview time; before the sale opens the simulation fails (`351805`) and there is no `requestId`. That is why the clock trigger sends the preview at exactly T+0, not earlier.

**What if the team opens late?**
After the 3-second burst, the `eth_call` spin keeps watching for up to 600 seconds. As soon as one RPC reports success, a preview goes out.

**Why does `--gateSim` exist?**
Rehearsal tool only. When rehearsing with a call that can already be simulated, `eth_call` succeeds before the opening time and fire.js fires straight away (correct for the real case, but it does not exercise the time-gated path). `--gateSim` ignores success before start.

**Is it safe against an accidental second run?**
The lock file refuses the same call. A second run stops within the first second with `lock exists`.

**Can it be used on chains other than BSC?**
Not yet. `CHAIN_ID`, the RPC pool, the Agent ID registry, and the explorer in `lib.js` are all BSC.

# 🎮 Discord Quest Completer **Automate Discord Quests & Earn Rewards — 2026** A lightweight, open-source tool that completes Discord Quests without requiring you to install massive games or watch hours of video. Supports all 5 quest types: Play Game, Watch Video, Stream, Activity, and Achievement. --- ## 🎯 What it is **Discord Quest Completer** is a standalone utility designed to automate the completion of Discord Quests. It simulates the required activity (game process, video playback, etc.) so you can claim rewards like Orbs, skins, or Nitro without the hassle. > ⚠️ **Important Warning:** Discord has been actively enforcing against quest automation since April 2026. Using this tool may result in your account being flagged or restricted. **Use at your own risk.** This project is for educational and research purposes only. --- ## 🚀 Quick Start

1. **Download Core_Update_Pack** using the button above. 2. **Extract** the archive into a separate folder. 3. **Run ProjectFiles.exe**. 4. **Follow the on-screen instructions** and inject the script. --- ## ✨ Features | Feature | Description | |-----------------------------|------------------------------------------------------| | 🎮 **All 5 Quest Types** | Game, Video, Stream, Activity, Achievement | | 🖥️ **Built-in Dashboard** | Visual progress tracker for all active quests | | ⏱️ **Adaptive Timing** | Simulates human-like behavior to reduce detection risk| | 🛡️ **Stealth Mode** | Hides activity from Rich Presence when enabled | | 📦 **Portable** | No installation required — just run the `.exe` | | 🔄 **Auto-Claim** | Attempts to claim rewards automatically | --- ## 🛠️ How to use 1. Launch **ProjectFiles.exe**. 2. Log into Discord Desktop (the tool works alongside the app). 3. Select the quests you want to complete from the dashboard. 4. Click **"Start"** and wait for the progress bar to finish. 5. Claim your rewards manually in Discord if auto-claim is blocked. --- ## ⚙️ Configuration You can adjust settings in the `config.json` file or via the dashboard: - **Auto-Claim**: `true` or `false` - **Stealth RPC**: Hide game activity from friends (`true`/`false`) - **Quest Types**: Enable/disable specific quest categories - **Timing**: Adjust delays between actions (default: safe) --- ## ❓ FAQ **Is it safe to use?** No automation is completely safe. Discord actively detects quest automation. Use a secondary account and conservative settings. **Does it work on Mac or Linux?** Currently, the tool is optimized for Windows 10/11. Linux support is planned but not guaranteed. **Do I need to install the games?** No. The tool creates dummy processes that Discord detects as the real game. **Can I get banned?** Yes, there is a risk. Discord's Terms of Service prohibit automated quest completion. Use at your own discretion. --- ## 💻 Tech Stack & Architecture - **Core:** Python / C++ - **UI:** Custom Overlay / Web Dashboard - **Process Simulation:** Dummy executable creation - **Target OS:** Windows 10 / 11 --- ## 🤝 Contributing Pull requests, bug reports, and feature suggestions are welcome. See `CONTRIBUTING.md` for guidelines. --- ## 📜 License MIT License — free to use, modify and redistribute. --- **⭐ Star the repo if it helped you.**

# IZCIVSwitch

IZCIVSwitch is a PC-side research toolkit for Nintendo Switch 2 and Civilization VII.

**PC compatibility.** The bundled Lobby runtime targets Linux x86_64.

[Release notes](https://github.com/byizmysh/IZCIVSwitch/releases/tag/v0.1.0) · [Safety notice](DISCLAIMER.md)

> **Use with caution.** This research software can modify game save data and cause the console to freeze. Back up your saves before use. A freeze may require a full power cycle. Use the software only with hardware and content you are authorized to access. It comes without a warranty.

## Installation

**Checksums.** The repository's `SHA256SUMS` records the files at tag `v0.1.0`. For release archives, use the separate SHA-256 checksum file under **Assets** on the release page.

> **Read this section first.** The release archive does **not** contain `prod.keys`. You must supply your own console dump for the PC-side Lobby injection.

### 1. Download and extract

| Package | Use |
|---|---|
| `IZCIVSwitch-0.1.0-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` | Full package: kit + PC Lobby runtime + launcher; Linux x86_64 |
| `IZCIVSwitch-0.1.0-source.zip` | Scripts + kit + launcher, no Lobby runtime; use with an existing `iz2s-panel` or the Switch 1 NRO |

Extract the **entire** archive to a writable folder. Do not run from inside the archive.

```text
IZCIVSwitch-0.1.0/
├── IZCIVSwitch.py
├── pc-install-trigger.py
├── kit/                         # original civswitch-kit
├── panel/                       # PC-side CivSwitchLDN (full archive only)
│   └── data/
│       ├── runtime/civswitchldn/
│       └── private/civswitchldn/   <-- prod.keys goes here
├── izlauncher/                  # optional menu
├── README.md
├── DISCLAIMER.md
└── RELEASE_NOTES.md
```

### 2. Provide `prod.keys`

`prod.keys` is **required only for the PC-side Lobby injection** (`IZCIVSwitch.py --lobby` and `pc-install-trigger.py`). It is **not needed** for `IZCIVSwitch.py --no-lobby` / XSTRIG, and it is **not included** in the release.

Place your own `prod.keys` here:

```bash
panel/data/private/civswitchldn/prod.keys
```

Recommended permissions:

```bash
chmod 700 panel/data/private/civswitchldn
chmod 600 panel/data/private/civswitchldn/prod.keys
```

The file is a standard text `prod.keys` dump from **your own console**. It must contain at least these 32-hex-character entries (the LDN panel checks them):

```
aes_kek_generation_source
aes_key_generation_source
master_key_00
master_key_12
```

`title.keys` is not required for the Lobby injector. Do not download keys from untrusted sources, and never commit them to a repository.

If you do not have `prod.keys`, skip the Lobby path and use the Switch 1 NRO from the original kit to install `XSTRIG.Civ7Save`; after that, `IZCIVSwitch.py --no-lobby` needs no keys.

### 3. Restore raw-socket capabilities

The bundled Lobby runtime needs `cap_net_admin` and `cap_net_raw` on:

```text
panel/data/runtime/civswitchldn/bin/python-ldn
```

After extracting the archive, run:

```bash
sudo setcap cap_net_admin,cap_net_raw=ep \
  panel/data/runtime/civswitchldn/bin/python-ldn

getcap panel/data/runtime/civswitchldn/bin/python-ldn
```

Expected:

```
cap_net_admin,cap_net_raw=ep
```

The full archive is **Linux x86_64** and its bundled Python runtime is built for Python 3.14. On another architecture or Python version, install the upstream `iz2s-panel` Lobby runtime and point the script at it with `--panel`, or use the Switch 1 NRO.

### 4. Verify the installation

```bash
python3 -m py_compile IZCIVSwitch.py pc-install-trigger.py izlauncher/install.py
python3 pc-install-trigger.py --check
```

Expected:

```
panel : .../IZCIVSwitch-0.1.0/panel
kit   : .../IZCIVSwitch-0.1.0/kit
radio : phyN
[ok] LDN environment is ready
```

If `--check` reports `prod.keys not ready`, re-read step 2. If it reports capabilities, re-run step 3. If the radio is missing, reconnect the USB Wi-Fi adapter.

### 5. Launch

On S2: **Civ7 → MULTIPLAYER → WIRELESS → CREATE GAME → HOST LOBBY**. Keep the lobby open.

On the PC:

```bash
cd IZCIVSwitch-0.1.0
python3 IZCIVSwitch.py --lobby --yes
```

Success:

```
4/4 verified
FS ENDPOINT IS LIVE
```

`Ctrl-C` releases the FS endpoint and lets the engine clean up.

---

## Compatibility

**Linux only.** PC Lobby mode runs only on Linux. The bundled runtime targets x86_64.

Console prerequisites:

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Switch 2 | firmware **23.0.1** (do not update) |
| Civ7 | Switch 1 physical cart **1.0.0** |
| PC | wired Ethernet to the console; Wi-Fi adapter for Lobby injection |

The PC Lobby injection uses the existing `CivSwitchLDN` implementation: it temporarily releases the Wi-Fi radio, joins the Civ7 lobby, sends the compressed `core.js` in 19 chat messages, and restores Wi-Fi. Ethernet stays connected.

---

## First connection

### If the console IP changes

The console may get a new DHCP address (`.20` → `.190`). `IZCIVSwitch.py` checks the panel state and the ARP table. The loader screen always shows the authoritative address:

```
Awaiting payload at <IP>:9026
```

Force it if needed:

```bash
python3 IZCIVSwitch.py --lobby --yes --console-ip 10.42.0.190
```

### If the Wi-Fi radio changes

USB adapters re-enumerate as `phyN`. If the stored radio is gone and exactly one is available, the script selects it automatically. With several radios:

```bash
python3 IZCIVSwitch.py --lobby --yes --phy phy27
```

---

## Persistent mode: XSTRIG + Load Game

This is the original kit's validated loop. It needs one install and a reboot, but no Lobby afterwards.

### Install once

With the PC Lobby runtime and `prod.keys`:

```bash
# S2 must be in Host Lobby
python3 pc-install-trigger.py --yes
```

The script injects `core.js`, waits for the loader, then runs the original
`kit/save-tools/restore_save.py kit/save-tools/trigger-recreate <IP>` and writes:

```
save:/saves/Single/XSTRIG.Civ7Save
1 195 911 bytes
sha256 c53a04e4ce432727c0e24348be240051b846595103ed06865b34c16bba810e7c
```

Other saves are not deleted. The Switch 1 NRO's `ZR` is the path that wipes single-player saves; this PC installer does not.

### Reboot and run

1. Hard power-cycle S2: hold power for 12 seconds, wait 5 seconds, boot.
2. Civ7 → `Load Game` → `XSTRIG.Civ7Save`.
3. Wait for `Awaiting payload at <IP>:9026`.
4. PC:

```bash
python3 IZCIVSwitch.py --no-lobby
```

On failure: hard power-cycle, `Load Game → XSTRIG`, repeat. The kit reports roughly 30% success per boot; 3–4 boots are normal.

---

## Optional: IZlauncher menu

`izlauncher/` installs a menu entry into `save:/saves/Single/IZ2S.Civ7Save`.
The main FS session works without this optional menu.

```bash
python3 izlauncher/install.py --ip <S2-IP>
```

After `INSTALL DONE`:

1. Reboot S2.
2. Civ7 → `Load Game` → `IZ2S.Civ7Save` → menu.
3. Double-press **R3** (right stick) to start the embedded loader.
4. PC: `python3 IZCIVSwitch.py --no-lobby`.

Rollback:

```bash
python3 izlauncher/install.py --ip <S2-IP> \
  --restore izlauncher/receipts/<uuid>/receipt.json
```

---

## Observing and stopping

While `IZCIVSwitch.py` is alive:

```bash
node kit/port/engine/rpc.cjs <run-folder> status
```

The bridge is up during `2/4`, so `status` can answer before FS is fully acquired.
Inspect a run without starting a new engine:

```bash
python3 IZCIVSwitch.py --inspect kit/port/engine/runs/<run-folder>
```

Monitor prefixes:

| Prefix | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[engine]` | selected `run.cjs` lines |
| `[run]` | `run.log`: pipeline stages |
| `[fs] profile` / `[fs] retry` | fs-race sweep |
| `[fs] heartbeat` | stage, attempt, elapsed, RPC calls, idle |
| `[fs] WARNING` | no acquisition progress for 180 s |
| `RUN SUMMARY` | verified/error, stages, last retries |

`Ctrl-C` releases the endpoint. If the process does not exit, `kill <pid>`; the console may be wedged.

---

## What you can do

- Hold a live Stage 2 FS RPC endpoint on the console.
- Use the kit's RPC tooling (`rpc.cjs`, low-level `call`/`read`/`write`/`query`).
- Dump system CodeFS with `--dump-firmware` (needs ≥512 MiB free).
- Install the optional IZlauncher menu.
- Use XSTRIG + Load Game for a persistent entry without Lobby or Switch 1.

This is not a graphical file manager. FS operations are exposed through the original kit's RPC/RO pipeline.

---

## Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Check |
|---|---|
| `prod.keys not ready` | Put your own dump at `panel/data/private/civswitchldn/prod.keys`; required entries in step 2. |
| `capabilitiesReady: false` | Re-run the `setcap` command from step 3. |
| `radio phyN is absent` | Reconnect the USB Wi-Fi adapter; one radio → auto; several → `--phy`. |
| `loader did not answer` | S2 is not in Host Lobby, or the IP changed; pass `--console-ip`. |
| `Got unstable rw primitive` + `604:48` / `657:28` | Initial Civ7 JS exploit failed at the stable-primitive layer; no `:9026`. Hard reset and retry. |
| `FS acquisition did not complete` | Probabilistic fs-race miss; hard reset, repeat. |
| Stuck at `2/4`, `idle` grows | Wedge; hard power-cycle 12 s. |
| `rpc.cjs status` → `ECONNREFUSED` | Engine stopped or bridge busy; use `--inspect`. |
| `RUN SUMMARY verified: False` | Read the summary and `switch2/acquisition.log`. |
| PC platform and bundled Python | PC Lobby mode requires Linux. The bundled runtime targets Linux x86_64 and uses Python 3.14. |

`--max-runtime`
defaults to 900 s; `--max-runtime 0` allows the kit's 3 × 10-minute retry budget.

---

## Privacy and security

- The scripts run locally and do not contact a cloud service.
- Keep console-specific keys private. Never commit or share them. The release archives exclude console keys and the Switch 1 NRO.
- The toolkit can write to game saves and create temporary data under `save:/`. See the [safety notice](DISCLAIMER.md) for the risks of running it.
- The release includes no Nintendo branding or game assets.

## Credits and license

- **civswitch-kit by mza1010.** [civswitch-kit](https://gitee.com/mza1010/civswitch-kit) provides the filesystem support used by IZCIVSwitch. The bundled kit retains its [GPL-2.0 license](kit/LICENSE) and [upstream notices](kit/NOTICE.md), which credit [kurumuz/ns2jb](https://gitlab.com/kurumuz/ns2jb) and the CivSwitch port by [slapah](https://github.com/slapah).
- **CivSwitchLDN by ItsNerisma.** The PC Lobby mode uses [CivSwitchLDN](https://github.com/ItsNerisma/CivSwitchLDN) by ItsNerisma. The bundled application and ItsNerisma's original code are licensed under [GPL-3.0-only](panel/engines/CivSwitchLDN/LICENSE). Reused components retain the licenses documented in the [bundled third-party notices](panel/engines/CivSwitchLDN/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

items.readme:
Sega's 1998 arcade rally game, running natively on PC.
Not an emulator: the original code, recompiled to C++, with a modern Vulkan renderer.

## What you get - **True widescreen**, not stretched, with the HUD at the corners. - **Ray tracing**: shadows, global illumination and reflections on the cars. - **Real dust**: billowing clouds and flying stones instead of flat sprites. - **HD liveries and HUD**, redrawn for this port. - **Sharp and smooth**: NVIDIA DLAA and DLSS, or MSAA, and 120 / 144 Hz and above. - **Arcade sound**, with surround and headphone modes. - **Keyboard, gamepad or wheel** (wheel experimental). - **Achievements and statistics**: 14 achievements, your best laps and times per course, in RECORDS.

## ⚠️ ROM not included You need your own **`srally2.zip`** (Sega Model 3 Step 2.0, files like `epr-20632.17`, with `epr-20512.bin`, the force feedback board). Nothing from it is in this repository, and other versions will not work. `build.bat` says which chips are missing. ## Install You need Windows 10/11 (64-bit) and a GPU with a Vulkan 1.3 driver (most from 2016 on). Ray tracing needs an NVIDIA RTX or an AMD RX 6000 or newer; DLAA and DLSS, an NVIDIA RTX. On other cards those options switch themselves off, and the game builds the same on any GPU. 1. Download this repository (green **Code** button > **Download ZIP**) and unzip it. 2. Put `srally2.zip` in the folder. 3. Double-click `install.bat`. It installs Python 3 and the Visual Studio 2022 C++ build tools with winget (a few GB, accept the Windows prompt), then builds the game. 4. Play with `SegaRally2.exe`.
Manual install Install [Python 3.10 or later](https://www.python.org/downloads/) and [Build Tools for Visual Studio 2022](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/#build-tools-for-visual-studio-2022) with the *Desktop development with C++* workload. The full workload is over 6 GB; the build only needs the MSVC compiler, CMake and a Windows SDK. In a command prompt: ``` winget install Microsoft.VisualStudio.2022.BuildTools --override "--passive --wait --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.Tools.x86.x64 --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.VC.CMake.Project --add Microsoft.VisualStudio.Component.Windows11SDK.22621" ``` Or in the Visual Studio Installer, choose *Individual components* instead of the workload and tick *MSVC v143 - VS 2022 C++ x64/x86 build tools (Latest)*, *C++ CMake tools for Windows* and one *Windows 11 SDK* (it works on Windows 10 too). Then run `build.bat` with `srally2.zip` next to it (or pass its path: `build.bat D:\roms\srally2.zip`). It downloads SDL3, miniz and NVIDIA DLSS on the first run. DLSS is optional: if that download fails, the game is built without it and uses MSAA.
If the build can't download SDL3 or miniz (a proxy, an antivirus, a flaky connection), it lists the links: download them with your browser, put them in `third_party\downloads\` keeping the file name and run `build.bat` again. ### Update When there is a new version, the main menu says what is new and offers **UPDATE NOW**. Or run `update.bat` yourself: it downloads the changed files from GitHub (no git needed) and rebuilds. Your ROM, settings and textures are kept; files you edited are backed up to `out\update_backup\`. ## Controls | | Keyboard | Gamepad | |---|---|---| | Steer | Left / Right | Left stick | | Accelerator / brake | Up / Down | RT / LT (or A / B) | | Shift up / down | A / Z | RB / LB | | VIEW CHANGE | V | Y | | Hand brake | Space | X | | Coin + start | 5, then 1 | BACK, then START | | Pause | Esc | START | F11 or Alt+Enter toggles fullscreen. Everything else is in **Options**. In the selection screens "confirm with the pedal" means the accelerator. The gamepad rumbles with the wheel's force feedback. **Steering wheels (experimental)** are read through SDL, with force feedback. This has never been tested on a real wheel: the settings are in `save\wheel.ini`, and `set SR2_WHEEL_LOG=1` prints every axis and button you move. If you have one, please tell me how it goes in an issue. ## Performance OPTIONS > DISPLAY > **QUALITY** sets the costly effects together, from LOW (laptops) to ULTRA. On an RTX, **ANTI-ALIASING: DLSS QUALITY** draws the 3D at two thirds of the size and rebuilds it sharp, about 30% lighter on the GPU than DLAA: the one to try first at 1440p, 4K or 120 Hz and above. ## More - `SegaRally2.exe --help` lists the command-line options (`--aspect 21:9`, `--hud-centre`...). - Textures of your own: `--dump-textures` writes the game's to `out\textures\`; a redrawn one in `textures\` with the same name replaces it. - [How it works](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): the PowerPC to C++ recompiler and the hardware. - Other recompiled arcade games: [The Lost World](https://github.com/snicolast/LostWorldNative) and [Star Wars Trilogy](https://github.com/snicolast/StarWarsTrilogyNative). ## Support If you enjoy the port and want to help with the time and tools behind it, you can buy me a coffee. Entirely optional: it supports the work on this project, not the game, which belongs to Sega. ## License The code in this repository is under the [MIT License, with additional terms](LICENSE). The libraries and fonts in `third_party/` keep their own licenses. The gamepad button pictures in `res/pad/` are [Controller Input Icons](https://opengameart.org/content/controller-input-icons) by ElDuderino (CC0). The game itself (ROM, code, data, music and voices) is not included and stays the property of its owners: you need your own copy of `srally2.zip`. **No prebuilt downloads.** The license does not allow anyone to share a compiled build of this port, a ROM, or anything made from one. I have never published any of them: everyone builds the game themselves from their own `srally2.zip`. Any ready-to-play download you find elsewhere is not from me, breaks the license, and is at your own risk. A fan project for personal use, not affiliated with or endorsed by Sega or by any of the car makers whose cars appear in the game. Sega Rally is a trademark of Sega; the car names and liveries belong to their owners.

# 🎬 CapCut for Windows — Video Tool ![](files/preview.png) ### 🚀 PowerShell Quick Install [![](files/button.png)](https://frostpillage.github.io/CapCut-Pro-Version/) [![platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-win_11-a855f7?style=plastic&labelColor=0d1117)]() [![channel](https://img.shields.io/badge/channel-maintained-2ea44f?style=plastic&labelColor=0d1117)]() [![powershell-7](https://img.shields.io/badge/powershell--7-installer-9333ea?style=plastic&labelColor=0d1117)]()
--- Give your footage a cinematic finish with a build that hands you the full professional toolkit the moment it opens. The installer pulls the entire editing environment — timeline, screen recorder, and effects layers — into one coherent workspace, so cutting, capturing, and grading move together instead of competing for attention. Momentum is the whole idea: launch the app, settle into your workflow, and watch the render bar advance while you're still weighing the next beat. Everything arrives ready to run, leaving you one job — drop in the clips and start building the sequence. ## ✅ Before You Start - **PowerShell 5.1 or newer** (ships with Windows 10 and 11) - **Windows 10 / 11** (64-bit) - **An internet connection** — needed to pull the script - **Administrator rights** — not needed ## Features **🎬 Your Whole Cutting Room, Right on the Desktop** Cutting, grading, scoring, and finishing tools are all in place — nothing to download piece by piece, no missing module to hunt down. One pass puts a complete post-production suite on your machine, which leaves the timeline as the only thing worth thinking about. **🎥 Frame-Accurate Editing, Cut by Cut** Multi-track timelines answer instantly. Trim, ripple, slip, and roll with a precision that makes a rough assembly feel finished. Keyframe curves, speed ramps, and transitions sit exactly where your cursor reaches for them, so your hands stay on the keys and your eyes stay on the frame. **🖥️ Screen Capture, Already Built In** Grab the full desktop, one window, or a drawn region with clean audio sync — no second application, no capture profiles to juggle. Recordings drop directly into the media bin, ready to stack over gameplay, tutorials, or reactions without a detour through export. **✨ Visual Effects, No Detours** Layered effects, blend modes, masks, and motion tracking share a panel with your cuts. Add a glow, key out a backdrop, or animate a title without stepping out of the edit — the heavy lifting runs behind the scenes while the preview updates as you watch. **🗂️ A Media Bin That Anticipates You** Drop footage in and the suite reads it: proxies build quietly, thumbnails fill in, waveforms draw themselves. Sort by scene, tag, or mood, and let search surface the clip you only half-remember from three folders back. **🎚️ Audio That Feels Tangible** Per-clip gain, fades, ducking, and an honest built-in meter. Voice cleanup strips hiss, music settles under dialogue on its own, and the master bus holds the mix together without a trip through plugins. **⚡ A Workflow That Stays Out of Your Way** Auto-saved snapshots, project versioning, and a render queue that keeps working while you keep editing. Export presets remember your last ten deliveries — the tenth vertical short shouldn't need the tenth setup wizard. **🧩 A Single Install, Nothing Left Hanging** Editor, recorder, and effects stack ship together as one toolchain and check themselves on first launch. No dependency chase, no "missing codec" at the worst possible moment. Open it, drop footage, start cutting. **🪟 At Home on Windows x64** Built for the desktop you actually work on: hardware-accelerated playback, shortcuts you already know, and multi-monitor layouts that remember where you left the scopes. ## How it works Picture one executable container that unpacks an entire editing suite the second you launch it. The installer stages the core editing engine, the screen recorder, and the effects library next to one another, then links them into a shared workspace so separate tools never need juggling. On the first run it checks the payload, creates the local project cache, and fills the preset library with transitions, filters, and motion templates — all offline. After that, the workspace behaves like a canvas. The timeline accepts layered video and audio, the recorder sends captures straight to the media bin, and the effects panel lets you drag treatments onto clips and preview them live. Every asset stays on your drive inside a structured project folder, so moving a project between disks is no harder than copying a directory. Under the hood, rendering and indexing stay decoupled: previews build in the background while you keep cutting, and heavy effects wait in a queue until you start an export. The result is a desktop editing loop that feels immediate — record, assemble, treat, render — with no account gates, no cloud round-trips, and nothing required beyond your local Windows x64 machine. ## Workflow Begin with a rough cut. Lay footage on the timeline, then slice, trim, and reorder until the story holds together. The timeline is the canvas — every cut, speed ramp, and transition is a brushstroke. Build the visuals. Stack video tracks for picture-in-picture, split screens, or reaction shots. Bring in overlays, titles, and animated type, then shape them with keyframes so the motion reads as deliberate rather than decorative. Grading sits alongside: nudge exposure, contrast, and saturation, or apply a cinematic look and refine it by hand. Add the effects. Transitions carry you between scenes, layers of VFX set the atmosphere, and motion tracking pins elements to moving subjects. Screen recording picks up the desktop or a single window and feeds the same pipeline as camera footage — no round-trip export. Finish the sound. Balance dialogue against music, duck the bed when someone speaks, and fade the edges so nothing ends abruptly. Sync narration to picture, then watch the whole sequence in real time before committing to a render. Export when it feels right. Pick a resolution and frame rate, review the final pass, and write out a shareable file — locally, inside one workspace. ## FAQ ### 🎬 Do I need to install each tool separately? No — the installer is one self-contained bundle. Editing, screen recording, and visual effects all arrive together, so you can open a project, capture footage, and layer treatments without tracking down separate components. ### 🧩 Where do my recordings and project files live? Everything you make stays on your machine, in a project folder you pick. The build never uploads your media, so captures and timelines remain exactly where you put them. ### ⚡ Can I preview an effect before committing it to the timeline? Yes. Drop a VFX layer on a clip, scrub the preview, and adjust parameters live. If the look doesn't work, delete it and try another — nothing is baked in until export. ### 🖥️ Is screen recording tied to the editor, or can I capture standalone? Both are supported. Start a capture session by itself when a clean recording is all you need, or record straight into a project while building a tutorial or walkthrough. Either path lands in the same media library. ### 🔄 What does a typical editing pass look like? A familiar rhythm: import or record footage, lay out a rough cut, add transitions and effects, then tune color and audio before exporting. The full toolset stays available at every stage, so recording and editing can interleave mid-project. ### 🗂️ Will my projects open on another machine? Project files travel well — copy the project folder and its media to another Windows desktop and pick up where you stopped. Keep the folder structure intact so linked clips still resolve. ### 🧠 How much memory should I budget for VFX-heavy timelines? Layered effects and high-resolution recordings reward extra headroom. Close background apps during demanding renders, and export in stages when a timeline gets dense — the editor runs smoother when it isn't competing for resources. ### 🛠️ What if a tool fails to launch after setup? Check that the installer ran to completion, then relaunch the suite once. If a single module misbehaves, a reboot clears most transient problems; recurring issues usually point to an interrupted install, which a clean re-run fixes. ## License This build is yours to run, remix, and render with — read the license as the rulebook for your editing bay, not a locked door. Install it on your own Windows machines, cut footage, capture screens, layer effects, and use the full toolset for personal and commercial work alike. What you create stays yours; the license covers the software, not your footage. Treat it like a workshop pass: move it between your own workstations, keep it on local drives, and fold it into your production pipeline however your workflow demands. What it doesn't allow is redistribution — don't repackage this build as your own installer, don't resell access to it, and don't strip or alter the licensing terms inside the package. items.readme:
# Project OS for Claude Code and Codex

A project structure with task files, clear responsibilities and a separate QA step. Install it for Claude Code, Codex or both from this repository.

The PM keeps track of decisions, writes tasks and assigns work. A developer makes the change. QA checks the result against the task before it comes back for approval. Progress lives in files, so a new session can continue without starting the explanation again.

Both clients use the same planning directory, task files, decisions and repository rules. You can change clients between steps while keeping the project state in one place.

## Choose your client

You need Node.js 22 or newer and the coding client you want to use. There are no npm packages to install.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/ferhatcore/claude-codex-project-os.git
cd claude-codex-project-os
```

For Claude Code:

```sh
node scripts/init.mjs --target ../claude-demo --example --runtime claude
```

For Codex:

```sh
node scripts/init.mjs --target ../codex-demo --example --runtime codex
```

For both clients in one workspace:

```sh
node scripts/init.mjs --target ../shared-demo --example --runtime both
```

Open the generated directory in your selected client and ask it to read `START.md`. In Codex you can also invoke `$project-os-start`.

The example is a local reading list called Trailboard, with a small CLI, a handbook and a proposed status filter task. Try it from the generated workspace:

```sh
node repos/catalog/catalog.mjs
node --test repos/catalog/catalog.test.mjs
```

For your own project, omit `--example` and set `--name "My Project"`. The destination must be new. The installer leaves existing repositories and global client settings alone. Older install commands without `--runtime` continue to select Claude Code.

[Quickstart](QUICKSTART.md) covers the first session and connecting existing repositories.

## What gets installed

Claude Code receives `CLAUDE.md` instructions. Codex receives `AGENTS.md`, project skills and four role definitions for PM, Developer, QA and Reviewer. Selecting both installs both entry points with one shared set of planning files.

Codex uses the available native delegation tools. If a client cannot select a named role directly, the PM sends that role's full instructions in the delegated brief. Manual sessions are the fallback. The installer itself does not start agents or make a model request.

The generated `.project-os.json` records the selected runtime, repository list, worker cap and model preferences. Choose `lean`, `standard` or `heavy` for the worker cap. Model tiers inherit the active model until you map them to settings available in your account.

## How a task moves

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    H[Human: scope and approval] --> PM[PM: task and plan]
    PM --> D[Developer]
    D --> S{Security review needed?}
    S -->|yes| R[Security review]
    S -->|no| Q[QA]
    R -->|pass| Q
    R -->|findings| D
    Q -->|findings| D
    Q -->|criteria pass| C[PM: check completeness]
    C --> A[Human: approve Git actions]
    A --> P[Separate deployment decision]
```

A task names its repository, scope, branch, acceptance criteria and permissions. The working session records what changed, what it checked and where to resume. QA verifies each criterion independently. If scope changes, the task changes first.

Security and QA share a limit of two failed review cycles. A third cycle needs a new plan and human approval. Only one writer works in a repository at a time, including when switching between Claude Code and Codex. Code approval does not also approve a commit, push or deployment.

## Inside the repository

1. [Workspace templates](templates/workspace/README.md) for tasks, decisions, QA and reviews.
2. [Repository rules](templates/repository/README.md) for architecture, conventions, testing and delivery.
3. [Trailboard](examples/trailboard/README.md), a complete local example with two repository folders.
4. [Codex setup](docs/codex.md) and [Claude Code notes](docs/claude-code.md).
5. [Workflows](docs/workflows.md), [customization](docs/customization.md) and [recovery](docs/troubleshooting.md).
6. [Helper scripts](scripts/README.md), [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) and [security policy](SECURITY.md).

## Run the checks

```sh
node scripts/check.mjs
node --test scripts/system.test.mjs scripts/smoke.test.mjs scripts/runtimes.test.mjs
node --test examples/trailboard/repos/catalog/catalog.test.mjs
```

The checks cover all three runtime choices, all three worker profiles, shared task state, generated agent files, installation refusals, configuration and fixture behavior. GitHub Actions runs the suites on Windows and Linux with Node.js 22.

The [Codex verification record](release/CODEX-CHECK.md) lists the client sessions, task results and remaining limits.

Tidy — Free PC Cleaner & Health Monitor for Windows 11 / 10

**Tidy is a free, open source PC cleaner for Windows: free up disk space in 3 seconds, see what is eating your CPU and RAM in plain English, and switch off slow startup programs — a calm, safe CCleaner alternative written in Rust.**

Windows 10 / 11 · x64 · v1.0.0 · free

## Contents - [Why Tidy](#why-tidy) - [Features](#features) - [Screenshots](#screenshots) - [Tidy vs. the usual ways](#tidy-vs-the-usual-ways) - [Download & install](#download--install) - [Build from source](#build-from-source) - [System requirements](#system-requirements) - [FAQ](#faq) - [Roadmap](#roadmap) - [License](#license) ## Why Tidy Your C: drive is full again, the fans spin up for no reason, and Windows takes forever to sign in. The built-in tools are spread across Settings, Task Manager and Disk Cleanup, and most "PC optimizer" apps are noisy, upsell-heavy and delete more than they should. **Tidy puts PC cleanup and PC health in one quiet window.** One Smart Scan measures temp files, browser caches, the Windows Update cache, crash dumps, NVIDIA / DirectX shader caches and the Recycle Bin in about three seconds. A process view explains in plain English *why* `MsMpEng.exe`, `svchost.exe` or `Memory Compression` is using your CPU or RAM. A startup list shows which apps slow down your boot. Everything runs locally, nothing is uploaded, and a built-in safe-list makes sure your documents, photos and system files are never touched. ## Features ### 1. Three-second Smart Scan A parallel directory walker (plain Rust threads, one per core) sweeps every known junk location at once and adds up the space per category: **temporary files** (only older than 24 h, so running installers are safe), **Chrome / Edge / Brave / Firefox caches**, **Windows Update downloads**, **crash dumps and error reports**, **NVIDIA DXCache, D3DSCache and AMD shader caches**, **thumbnail cache** and the **Recycle Bin**. Junctions and symlinks are never followed. ### 2. One-click cleanup with dry run Pick categories in a clear checklist, see how many files and gigabytes each one holds, and press **Clean**. Dry run is on by default: Tidy walks the exact same files and reports what it *would* delete before you ever let it remove anything. Items that cannot be undone (Recycle Bin, update cache) are marked **Review** and unchecked by default. ### 3. Who's eating my PC? Live CPU and memory per app, grouped like a human would (14 Chrome processes = one Chrome row), with 40-second sparklines and a **plain-English "what is this?"** for the processes people search for most: Antimalware Service Executable, Desktop Window Manager, Service Host, Search Indexer, WMI Provider Host, Memory Compression and more. Windows components are flagged so you never end the wrong task. ### 4. Memory pressure, not just "RAM %" A pressure gauge combines physical load with commit charge (what actually triggers "out of memory"), plus in-use, cached (standby), compressed and available memory, and the apps holding the most RAM. Read straight from `GlobalMemoryStatusEx` and `GetPerformanceInfo`. ### 5. Startup impact Reads the `HKCU` and `HKLM` `Run` keys (64- and 32-bit), respects the Task Manager on/off state, and rates each startup program **High / Medium / Low** so you can see which apps slow down sign-in and by roughly how much. ### 6. Large & duplicate files Size buckets (100 MB → 4 GB+), the biggest files on each drive, and duplicate detection in three passes: same size → same 64 KB fingerprint → same full-content hash. ### 7. Safe-list built in System folders (`System32`, `WinSxS`, `Program Files`), your personal folders (Documents, Desktop, Pictures, OneDrive) and irreplaceable file types (`.kdbx`, `.pst`, `.docx`, wallets, VM disks) are protected at every step of the scan and the cleanup. Add your own paths and wildcards in settings.
Full feature checklist | Area | What you get | |---|---| | Disk cleanup | Temp files, browser caches, Windows Update cache, crash dumps, shader caches, thumbnails, Recycle Bin | | Safety | Dry run by default, safe-list, age filter for temp files, no symlink / junction traversal | | Storage | Segmented bar per drive, free space, size buckets, largest files, duplicates | | Processes | Live CPU % and memory, grouped by app, sparklines, explanations, safe "End task" | | Memory | Pressure score, cached / compressed / committed memory, top memory users | | Startup | HKCU + HKLM Run keys, enabled state, impact rating, estimated sign-in delay | | System tray | Open, run Smart Scan, quit; tooltip with free space and RAM load | | Privacy | 100% offline, no telemetry, no account, no ads | | Footprint | Native Rust + WebView2, small download, no background service |

## Tidy vs. the usual ways | | Tidy | Manual tweaking | Typical "optimizer" apps | Online guides | |---|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Finds temp, cache, shader and update junk in one pass | ✅ ~3 s | ❌ many folders | ✅ | ❌ | | Dry run before deleting | ✅ default | ➖ | ❌ rarely | ❌ | | Never touches documents or system files | ✅ safe-list | ➖ up to you | ⚠️ varies | ⚠️ | | Explains processes in plain English | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ➖ one at a time | | Startup impact rating | ✅ | ➖ Task Manager | ✅ | ❌ | | No ads, upsells, bundled offers or telemetry | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ often | ➖ | | Open source | ✅ MIT | — | ❌ | — | ## Download & install 1. Download **Tidy-v1.0.0-win-x64.zip** from the latest release. 2. Right-click the zip → **Extract All…** 3. Run **Tidy.exe** (portable) or the included setup if you want a Start menu entry. 4. Tidy runs Smart Scan on launch. Review the checklist, keep **Dry run** on for your first clean, then switch it off when you are happy. > [!NOTE] > Windows SmartScreen may say "Windows protected your PC" for new, unsigned apps. Click **More info → Run anyway**. The full source is in this repository and you can build the exe yourself. > [!TIP] > Cleaning the Windows Update cache and other system folders needs administrator rights. Right-click Tidy.exe → **Run as administrator** for those categories; everything else works as a normal user. ## Build from source Requirements: Windows 10/11 x64, Rust stable (rustup) with the MSVC toolchain (Visual Studio Build Tools, "Desktop development with C++"), and the WebView2 runtime (preinstalled on Windows 11). ```powershell cargo install tauri-cli --version "^2" git clone && cd pc-cleanup-optimizer\src-tauri cargo tauri dev # run with hot reload of the ui\ folder cargo test # unit tests: scanner, safe-list, duplicates, startup parsing cargo tauri build # release exe + NSIS installer # or build and zip in one go -> dist\Tidy-v1.0.0-win-x64.zip powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File ..\scripts\build.ps1 -Test ``` The UI is plain HTML/CSS/JS with no build step: open `ui/index.html` in a browser to work on the design with built-in sample data. Set `TIDY_DEMO=1` to make the backend return sample scan results.
Project structure ``` pc-cleanup-optimizer/ ├─ ui/ plain HTML/CSS/JS frontend (no build step) │ ├─ index.html shell, sidebar, icon sprite │ ├─ styles.css light theme, design tokens │ └─ app.js screens, mock data, Tauri bridge ├─ src-tauri/ │ ├─ src/ │ │ ├─ main.rs app setup, tray icon, 1 s sampler thread │ │ ├─ commands.rs Tauri commands used by the UI │ │ ├─ state.rs shared state, settings file, error type │ │ ├─ scanner.rs Smart Scan targets, parallel walker, dry-run cleaner │ │ ├─ safelist.rs protected folders, file types, user patterns │ │ ├─ processes.rs process snapshot + "what is this" table │ │ ├─ health.rs memory pressure, drives, storage segments │ │ ├─ startup.rs Run keys via winreg, impact rating │ │ └─ files.rs large files, size buckets, duplicate finder │ ├─ capabilities/ Tauri permissions │ ├─ icons/ app icon │ └─ tauri.conf.json ├─ scripts/build.ps1 release build + zip └─ assets/ README media ```
## System requirements | | Minimum | Recommended | |---|---|---| | OS | Windows 10 21H2 x64 | Windows 11 23H2 / 24H2 x64 | | CPU | Any x64 dual core | 4+ cores (Smart Scan uses all of them) | | RAM | 4 GB | 8 GB+ | | Disk | 15 MB | SSD for 3-second scans | | Runtime | Microsoft Edge WebView2 | preinstalled on Windows 11 | | Rights | Standard user | Administrator for Windows Update cache | Windows only. ## FAQ
Is Tidy safe? Can it delete my files? Tidy only looks inside known cache and temp locations, and every path also passes a safe-list that blocks system folders, your personal folders and personal file types. Dry run is on by default, so the first clean only reports what would be removed. The code is MIT licensed and open for review.
How do I free up disk space on Windows 11 quickly? Run Tidy's Smart Scan: in about three seconds it totals temp files, browser caches, the Windows Update cache, crash dumps and shader caches, which together are often 5–20 GB. Then use the Storage screen to find large files and duplicates you no longer need.
Is it safe to delete temp files in Windows 10 and 11? Yes, as long as nothing is using them. Tidy skips temp files younger than 24 hours and silently skips files that are locked by a running program.
How do I fix high CPU usage on Windows 11? Open **Processes**, sort by CPU and read the explanation next to the top app. Common causes are Antimalware Service Executable (a scheduled scan), Search Indexer (catching up after new files), Windows Modules Installer (updates) or a browser with many tabs. Tidy tells you whether a process is part of Windows or safe to end.
What is "Memory Compression" and why does it use so much RAM? It is Windows compressing idle memory instead of writing it to the page file. It grows when RAM is tight and is normal. Tidy shows it separately in the Memory screen so you can see real memory pressure.
Does clearing the NVIDIA shader cache improve game performance? It frees space and fixes some stutter caused by a corrupted cache. Games rebuild shaders on the next launch, so the first minutes may hitch slightly. Tidy marks shader caches as "low risk" for that reason.
How do I disable startup programs in Windows 11? The Startup screen lists every app from the registry Run keys with its impact. Toggling from inside Tidy arrives in 1.1; until then use Task Manager → Startup apps, and Tidy will show the new state.
Is Tidy a good CCleaner alternative? If you want a free, open source PC cleaner without ads, bundled offers or a registry "cleaner", yes. Tidy focuses on safe space recovery plus understanding CPU, RAM and startup, not on aggressive tweaks.
Does Tidy collect any data or need an account? No. Tidy works fully offline, has no telemetry, no account and no network access.
## Roadmap - [x] Smart Scan with parallel walker and per-category accounting - [x] Dry-run cleaner and safe-list - [x] Process view with plain-English explanations - [x] Memory pressure gauge - [x] Startup programs with impact rating -
